Answer: A
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1a) shows a well-defined, round soft-tissue mass projecting over the central tracheal air column (indicated by the arrow), which is characteristic of a benign tracheal tumor (such as a squamous papilloma or carcinoid) causing partial airway obstruction and wheezing. Options describing lung lobe masses or irregular malignant features do not match the specific central tracheal finding highlighted.
